format.summary: Student card text. Code fills {placeholders} with display values (digits and symbols) and shows a block or item only when its `when` is true. The rules engine decides every number; the card only formats them.
format.order: File order = the order on every card, for every tier and route (docs/SPEC.md, student card blocks): today_action, expedited, why, answer_sheet, documents, interview, after_approval, food_today, contact. The card builder sends, in this order, each block whose `when` is true and that has at least one item or row. Route table (check_content.py checks it): likely -> all nine (expedited only for an outlook of yes or maybe); every coordinator route except coordinator.parent_household -> today_action, why, answer_sheet, documents, interview, food_today, contact; coordinator.parent_household -> why, food_today, contact (that student applies as the parents' household, so the card says to talk to the coordinator first); other_help.* -> why, food_today, contact; info.already_receiving -> why, after_approval, contact; info.interview_waiting -> why, interview, contact. Block conditions use reason codes, so an info route shows the same blocks whatever its tier.
format.block: {id, tone, collapsed, when, title, title_by_tier?, title_by_reason?, intro?, columns?, items[] | rows[], sources[], verify?}. tone is one of default, accent, warning, muted (CardBlock.tone). collapsed is the block's starting state (CardBlock.collapsed): documents, interview and after_approval start collapsed, every other block starts open (docs/SPEC.md, student card blocks). Title: title_by_reason for the case's reason code, else title_by_tier for its tier, else title. items: {when, text}. rows (answer_sheet): {when, screen, question, answer}; screen stays in English in every language.
format.when: AND of the keys below; {} is always true. An OR is written with not: {"not": [{"not": [A, B]}]} means A or B. A case with no reason code yet (the call ended before a result) shows only the blocks whose `when` does not need one (food_today, contact).
format.renamed: items are the card's paragraphs (each item has its own when). The first-month line is the today_action item that uses {filed_on}, {first_month} and {month_label} (FirstMonth fields). irt_applies may be null when there is no estimate; then neither IRT item shows.
format.headline: headline and subhead: one per tier, plus likely_floor (the estimate is a floor), incomplete (the call ended before a result), and one per info route (keys info.already_receiving and info.interview_waiting), used when the case's reason code is an info route, whatever its tier.
format.verify: verify names an entry of unverified[]: the line avoids exact dates where its source is not confirmed, and the source is re-checked before a real pilot.
format.ui: Strings for the card page's own controls, the same as docs/UI_SPEC.md (card UI strings). ui.calendar = the 3 .ics events (days after the estimated filing day), as in docs/SPEC.md; they are calendar entries the student downloads, and refriGator sends nothing. ui.rules_label is CardView.rules_label in this language (the English text equals the rules table's label).

when_keys.tier: list of tiers: likely, coordinator, other_help
when_keys.reason: list of reason codes (the frozen list in docs/SPEC.md); true if the case's reason code is in it
when_keys.expedited: list of expedited outlooks: yes, maybe, no
when_keys.irt_applies: true or false: gross income at the estimate is at or under the 130% line (the rules table's irt_card_rule)
when_keys.at_max: true or false: the estimate equals the maximum amount for the household size
when_keys.flag: list of policy flags (e.g. abawd_possible, ta_ra_income_type); true if any is set
when_keys.has: slot name (or list): the slot has a value, from the student or a default
when_keys.answered: slot name (or list): the student gave this value (not assumed)
when_keys.positive: slot name (or list): value > 0, true, or not 'none'
when_keys.zero: slot name (or list): value is 0, false or 'none'
when_keys.slot: {slot: [canonical values]}: the slot's value is one of them
when_keys.not: list of conditions; true if none of them is true

filed_on.fill: FirstMonth.filed_on (estimated filing day), e.g. Fri, Oct 2

irt.fill: 130% line for the household size (rules table irt_130), e.g. $1,729

reviewed_at.fill: time the coordinator marked the case reviewed, e.g. 5:03 PM

items.text: Apply on BenefitsCal. To send your application today, you only need your name, where you live and your signature. The rest can come later.
How: fill in “Your Information”, then sign and submit. You can leave the other sections for later.
Why today? Your first month counts from the day the county gets your application. Our estimate: an application sent on a weekday before 5 PM counts that same day.
Our estimate: if you send it now, it counts from {filed_on}, and your first month may be about {first_month} for {month_label}.
You may get CalFresh within 3 days. The county checks this when you apply.
You might get CalFresh within 3 days. The county checks this when you apply.
Answer the emergency questions on BenefitsCal honestly. For this fast help, the county first needs to check who you are, so have your ID ready.

title_by_tier.coordinator: Why a person needs to check

items.text: Since June 2026, SF State bachelor's students taking 8 or more units meet CalFresh's student rule. Just say you're in a bachelor's program.
With fewer than 8 units, CalFresh's student rule doesn't apply to you.
With fewer units than half-time, CalFresh's student rule doesn't apply to you.
A work rule may apply: CalFresh may stop after 3 months in 3 years unless you work, volunteer or train at least 80 hours a month. The coordinator can check this with you.
As a grad student with a campus job, you meet CalFresh's student rule.
As a grad student with a TA or RA job, you meet CalFresh's student rule.
As a grad student with work-study, you meet CalFresh's student rule.
As a grad student who works 20 or more hours a week, you meet CalFresh's student rule.
As a grad student caring for a child under 6, you meet CalFresh's student rule.
As a grad student, you told us about a situation that meets CalFresh's student rule. The county will check it.
TA or RA pay counts as income when it is a wage. A fellowship or stipend may not count. The coordinator can check.
Financial aid, scholarships and student loans don't count as income.
Money from family or friends counts as income, even if it's for school.
Work-study pay doesn't count as income.
Rent that someone else pays to your landlord isn't income for you, but you can't count that part as your own cost.
You pay something for a place to stay, so the county can count a housing cost for you.
Your rent is high compared to your income, so your estimate is the highest amount for your household size.
With little or no income, your estimate is the highest amount for your household size.
You already get CalFresh, so your key dates are your SAR 7 report and your renewal (see “After approval”).
You already applied, so get ready for the county's phone interview (see “Your phone interview”).
If you applied before without getting CalFresh, the rules changed this year, so it's worth applying again.
You're under 22 and live with a parent, so CalFresh counts you and your family as one household. Talk to the SF State CalFresh coordinator first: they can help you apply together with your family.
You buy and cook food with others, so CalFresh may count them with you. A person needs to check who is in your household.
Grad students need to meet extra CalFresh student rules. A person needs to check which one fits you.
For programs that aren't a degree, like a credential or a certificate, a person needs to check CalFresh's student rules.
At your age, different CalFresh student rules apply. A person needs to check them with you.
Gig and self-employed pay is counted in a special way. A person needs to check it with you.
When you pay someone for both a room and meals, special CalFresh rules apply. A person needs to check them.
Your spouse is also a student, so a person needs to check how CalFresh counts your household.
CalFresh rules for your situation changed this year, so a person needs to check. We didn't save what you told us about it.
With a disability benefit, or at age 60 or older, different CalFresh rules apply. A person needs to check them.
One answer could change your result, so a person needs to check it before giving a number.
CalFresh rules for your situation are complicated, so we won't guess. We didn't save what you told us about your status.
Your income may be over the CalFresh limit for your household. The county decides.
With a campus meal plan of more than 10 meals a week, CalFresh works differently. If your meal plan changes, check again.
refriGator is built for SF State students. Your county's CalFresh office can help you.
For a household your size, our estimate may come out very low or at zero. The county decides.

rows.question: Last steps
rows.answer: Answer the 3-day (emergency) questions honestly. Pick the county where you live. Save your application number.

items.text: A photo ID. Your student ID works.
Proof of your address, like a lease or a bill.
No proof of address is needed if you don't have a fixed home.
Pay stubs from the last 30 days, or a letter from your boss.
Records of what you earned from gig or self-employed work.
Usually not needed — keep them handy in case the county asks: your class schedule and your financial aid papers.
You don't need papers to apply. When the county asks, upload them in BenefitsCal. A clear phone photo works. Save the upload receipt.
Not sure how to send them? Call the county: {county_phone}.
After you apply, the county sets up your interview. You can choose phone or in person. Plan for about an hour. A call may show up as “Unknown” or “Spam Likely.” Answer it.
No call yet? Call the county at {county_phone}, or talk to the SF State CalFresh coordinator.
Got a letter or a BenefitsCal message asking you to call? Call {county_phone} ({county_hours}) before the deadline.
They will ask about: who you live and eat with, your job and other money, your rent and bills, your classes and financial aid, and anything that changed.
From today's answers: work pays about {earned_monthly} a month.
From today's answers: others give you about {other_cash_monthly} a month.
From today's answers: your rent share is {rent_share} a month.
Your rights: a free interpreter, an in-person interview if you ask, bringing anyone you want, a decision within 30 days, and at least 10 days to send papers.
Missed the call? You'll get a letter called “Notice of Missed Interview” (CF 386). Call {county_phone} right away to set a new time. If you wait too long, you may have to apply again.
Asked for papers after the interview? Send them by the date on the request. You get at least 10 days.
Live outside San Francisco? Your own county handles your case. The phone numbers here are for San Francisco.
Your EBT card comes in the mail. Activate it before you use it.
Lost card? Call {ebt_phone}.
About 6 months in, the county sends a short report form called SAR 7. Fill it out and send it back by the date on the form.
About 12 months in, you renew with a form and an interview.
If your household's total income goes over {irt} a month, tell the county within 10 days.
You don't need to report income changes between reports. Report all your income on your SAR 7.
If you move, tell the county your new address so you get your letters.
Gator Groceries and the AS Food Pantry give free food to all SF State students, every week.
Where: Cesar Chavez Student Center, bottom floor (Rec and Dining Level). Hours change. See {pantry_url}.
Need meals now? SF State Basic Needs has emergency meal cards. See {meals_url}.
SF State CalFresh coordinator (CalFresh Help Clinic, Basic Needs), {coordinator_place}.
Email {coordinator_email} to book a time, or call {coordinator_phone}. Hours: {coordinator_hours}.
Your case code: {case_code}. Share it so they can find your answers.
San Francisco CalFresh (county): {county_phone}, {county_hours}.
In crisis? Call 988 anytime. In an emergency, call 911.

unverified.what: Checked on the live BenefitsCal site on 2026-10-01: the application sections and their order (Your Information, People, Household Details, Income, Expenses, Assets, Other Situations, Document Upload, Review & Submit) and the minimum to submit (name, where you live and a signature; date of birth only for cash aid; 'after that, you can submit your application at any time'). Not checked, because it needs typed answers: the exact button that skips to submit and the student-situation choices inside Household Details. The card does not name that button.

The interview call timing, the interview rights line, the missed-interview letter name (CF 386) and the papers line follow 7 CFR 273.2 and the CF 386 notice as summarized in the project research; the regulation text was not re-read on 2026-10-01. Until it is, the card gives no day count for the interview call, and the missed-call and papers lines give no deadline beyond 'right away' and 'at least 10 days'. BenefitsCal's application overview (live, 2026-10-01): for CalFresh you can choose a phone or in-person interview; plan for about an hour.

The documents list follows 7 CFR 273.2 (identity, address, income) and the SF State CalFresh Help Clinic page, which says the county may ask for a class schedule, financial aid letters and pay stubs after the interview. The county's own request decides what is needed; the list was not checked against a county checklist. BenefitsCal's application overview (live, 2026-10-01) lists proof of identity (a student ID works), proof of income and proof of expenses, and says documents are not needed to apply and can be uploaded later.
